texts.li: [founding] {FACTION} keep the day {DEAD} was founded, as the colony kept it when {PLACE} was its home, and this year they want the colony's people at the table for it. The invitation came from {HOST}, with a line at the bottom: the old seats are still there.

[founding,their:lowtech] A runner from {PLACE} brought word: {FACTION} light the fire on the day {DEAD} was founded, as the colony did, and they ask the colony's people to sit at it with them this year.

[handover] It is a year again since {DEAD} was handed over and {PLACE} became the town of {FACTION}, and they mark the day with a meal. {HOST} asks the colony's people to come and sit with the ones who stayed.
[handover,their:hightech] The message from {PLACE} is short: the anniversary of the hand-over, a dinner in the old common room, the colony's people invited. {HOST} signed it.
[founding] {HOST} sends word from {PLACE}: it is nearly {DEAD}'s day again, and {FACTION} would like to keep it with the colony's people at the table.
[founding] {FACTION} will keep the day {DEAD} was founded at {PLACE} this year, and {HOST} asks for the colony's people to be there.
[handover] {FACTION} remember the day {DEAD} became {PLACE}, and want the colony at their table for it this year. {HOST} asks that at least a few come.
[handover] On the day {DEAD} was handed over, {FACTION} sit down together at {PLACE}, and {HOST} asks the colony's people to sit with them this year.

li.label: Accept the invitation
li.outcome: Places will be set for the colony's guests at {PLACE}.

li.label: Decline with thanks
li.outcome: {FACTION} are sorry, and say they will keep the day all the same.

terms.li: At least two of the colony's people at {PLACE} by caravan within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing (it's about {TALE} away), staying for the day, about half a day at the town. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThe guests go home with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver, and {FACTION} will remember who came. If no one does, they'll notice that too.

accepted.li: The colony will send guests to {PLACE}. Form a caravan of at least two and send it there within {DAYS}.
[founding] The colony will keep {DEAD}'s day at {PLACE}. Send a caravan of at least two there within {DAYS}.

ready.li: The colony's guests have reached {PLACE} and been given the old seats at the table. Keep the caravan there until the day is over.
[handover] The colony's guests have reached {PLACE}, and the ones who stayed came out to meet them. Keep the caravan there until the meal is over.
The colony's guests are at {PLACE}, and room has been made for them at the table. Keep the caravan there until the day is over.

reminder.li: The day at {PLACE} is coming, and the colony's guests haven't arrived.

done.li: [attended,founding] The colony's guests kept {DEAD}'s day at {PLACE} with {FACTION}, at the tables the colony built, and came home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[attended,handover] The colony's guests sat with the ones who stayed at {PLACE} and remembered the day {DEAD} was handed over. {FACTION} sent them home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[attended] The colony's guests were made welcome at {PLACE} and came home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[brief] The colony's guests reached {PLACE} but didn't stay to the end. {FACTION} were glad they came at all.
[attended,founding] {DEAD}'s day was kept at {PLACE} with the colony's guests among {FACTION}, and they came home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[attended,handover] The colony's guests and {FACTION} remembered together the day {DEAD} was handed over, and the guests came home with gifts: {ITEM}.

fail.li: [absent] {FACTION} kept the day at {PLACE} without the colony, with places set for its guests until late.
[absent] Nobody from the colony came to {PLACE} for the day, and {FACTION} noticed the empty seats.

cancelled.li: The invitation to {PLACE} no longer stands.
